Internal technologies, including the mobile application, backend services, machine-learning service, and database, are contained within the system boundary and should not be shown as external entities in this diagram. Their detailed relationships will be presented in the system architecture in Chapter 4\.

### **3.4.3 Use Case Analysis** {#3.4.3-use-case-analysis}

Use case analysis describes how human users and supporting external services interact with the Smart Bakery Food Waste Reduction System. The analysis identifies the functions available to the Bakery Manager and System Administrator and clarifies the participation of the Weather Service, Calendar/Holiday Service, and Push Notification Service. Three use case diagrams are prepared to prevent the complete system model from becoming overcrowded. The overall diagram presents the principal system functions, while separate diagrams provide more detailed views of the Manager and Administrator interactions. 

![][image7]  
*Figure 3.3: Overall System Use Case Diagram*

Figure 3.3 presents the overall interactions between the principal actors and the proposed system. Both the Bakery Manager and System Administrator can authenticate, manage their profiles, view dashboards and reports, and manage notifications according to their permissions. The Manager performs operational functions, including demand prediction, production recommendation, production confirmation, sales simulation, and surplus management. The Administrator manages the prediction model, inventory and product data, user accounts, system settings, external-service configurations, and audit information. The Weather Service and Calendar/Holiday Service provide contextual data for demand prediction and sales simulation, while the Push Notification Service supports the delivery of event-based background notifications.  
![][image8]  
*Figure 3.4: Manager Use Case Diagram*

Figure 3.4 provides a detailed representation of the Bakery Manager’s use cases. The Manager can generate and review next-day demand predictions, examine ingredient shortages, obtain production recommendations, and confirm the final production quantity. When changing a recommendation, the Manager can reduce or override the suggested quantity, after which the system records the final decision. The Manager can also initiate the sales simulation, review simulation results, manage leftovers through donation or waste recording, view reports and dashboards, and manage received notifications. Weather and calendar data are retrieved during prediction and simulation, while production feasibility is checked when generating a production recommendation.

![][image9]  
*Figure 3.5: Administrator Use Case Diagram* 

Figure 3.5 presents the functions available to the System Administrator. The Administrator manages users and roles, ingredients, bread categories, recipes, inventory batches, charity partners, bakery settings, system parameters, and external-service configurations. The Administrator can also initiate model retraining, review model-evaluation results, manage model versions, and restore a previous valid model where necessary. Inventory movements, inventory-quality issues, administrative notifications, system logs, and audit records can also be reviewed. These functions support data quality, access control, system configuration, traceability, and the maintenance of the prediction component.

|  | 7\. The system authenticates the credentials and verifies that the user account is active. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-01)**  |
|  | 8\. The system retrieves the authenticated user’s assigned role and permissions. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04)**  |
|  | 9\. The system establishes an authenticated session. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-01)**  |
|  | 10\. The system displays the appropriate dashboard and functions according to the user’s role. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04)**  |
| 11\. The user accesses the permitted system functions.  |  |
| **Alternative Flows of Events A1. Steps 3–4 – Required information is missing**If the email address or password is missing, the system displays a validation message and requests the user to complete the required fields. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-01) A2. Steps 6–7 – Invalid credentials**If the credentials are invalid, the system denies access, displays an authentication error and allows the user to retry. No authenticated session is created. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-01) A3. Step 7 – Account is inactive or access is restricted**If the account is inactive or restricted, the system denies access and displays an appropriate message. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04) A4. Steps 6–7 – Authentication service is unavailable**If the authentication service cannot be reached, the system displays an error message and allows the user to retry. No authenticated session is created. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-03) A5. Step 11 – User logs out**The authenticated user selects **Log Out**. The system terminates the current session, removes locally stored authentication information and returns the user to the login screen. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-02)** |  |

*Table 3.11: Use Case Specification for Generate Demand Prediction* 

| Use Case ID:  UC-DP-01 |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Use Case Name:** Generate Demand Prediction |  |
| **Actor:** Bakery Manager |  |
| **Supporting Actors:** Weather Service and Calendar/Holiday Service |  |
| **Brief Description:** The Bakery Manager initiates the generation of next-day sales predictions for active bread categories. The system uses historical sales patterns, temporal features, weather conditions, and calendar information to generate the predictions. |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. The Bakery Manager is logged in. 2\. At least one active bread category exists. 3\. The prediction configuration and cold-start rules are available. 4\. Historical sales records are available or the cold-start method can be applied. |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. The prediction results are stored for the applicable bread categories. 2\. Each prediction is associated with its date, confidence level, explanation, and model information. 3\. The prediction results are available for production-recommendation generation. |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Responses** |
| 1\. The Bakery Manager selects **Demand Prediction.**  | 2\. The system displays the demand-prediction screen and the next prediction date.  |
| 3\. The Bakery Manager selects **Generate Prediction**. | 4\. The system validates the prediction date, active bread categories, prediction configuration and available data. **(Requirement: FR-DP-05)**  |
|  | 5\. The system retrieves validated historical daily sales and generates lag sales, rolling averages, sales trends and same-weekday features. **(Requirement: FR-DP-01, FR-DP-02)**  |
|  | 6\. The system derives the day of the week, weekend status, month and monsoon season for the prediction date. **(Requirement: FR-DP-03)**  |
|  | 7\. The system retrieves weather and public-holiday information for the prediction date from the Weather Service and Calendar/Holiday Service. **(Requirement: FR-DP-04)**  |
|  | 8\. The system uses the active prediction model when sufficient valid historical sales data are available. Otherwise, it applies the configured cold-start method. **(Requirement: FR-DP-06, FR-DP-07)**  |
|  | 9\. The system generates the next-day sales prediction for each active bread category. **(Requirement: FR-DP-05)**  |
|  | 10\. The system calculates the confidence indicator and identifies the relevant factors influencing each prediction. **(Requirement: NFR-ACC-08)**  |
|  | 11\. The system stores the prediction date, predicted quantity, confidence indicator, supporting information and model version. **(Requirement: FR-DP-08)**  |
|  | 12\. The system displays the generated prediction details for each bread category. **(Requirement: FR-DP-08)**  |
| 13\. The Bakery Manager reviews the generated prediction details. |  |
| **Alternative Flows of Events A1. Step 4 – Invalid or incomplete prediction configuration** If no active bread category or valid prediction configuration is available, the system stops the operation, identifies the missing configuration and informs the Bakery Manager to contact the System Administrator. **(Requirement: FR-DP-05) A2. Step 8 – Insufficient historical sales data** If fewer than 30 distinct valid daily records per bread category are available, the system applies the configured cold-start method. The resulting prediction is identified as a cold-start prediction. **(Requirement: FR-DP-07) A3. Step 7 – External data cannot be retrieved** If weather or public-holiday information cannot be retrieved, the system informs the Bakery Manager and provides a retry option. Where permitted by the configured rules, the system may continue using available or default contextual information and shall identify the substituted information. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-03) A4. Steps 9–11 – Prediction generation or storage failure** If prediction generation or storage fails, the system records the error, displays a failure message and does not create an incomplete prediction record. The Bakery Manager may retry the operation. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01)** |  |

*Table 3.12: Use Case Specification for Manage Prediction Model*

| Use Case ID:  UC-DP-02  |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Use Case Name:** Manage Prediction Model |  |
| **Actor:** System Administrator  |  |
| **Supporting Actors:** – |  |
| **Brief Description:** The System Administrator manages the prediction-model lifecycle by manually initiating model retraining, reviewing evaluation results, activating a valid candidate model or restoring a previous valid model version. |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. The System Administrator is logged in. 2\. The Administrator has permission to manage prediction models. 3\. The model-management configuration is available.  |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. The selected model-management action is completed or cancelled without creating an incomplete model record. 2\. A newly trained model is stored as a candidate version and does not automatically replace the active model. 3\. The active model changes only after a valid candidate or previous version is confirmed for activation. 4\. Previous valid model versions remain available for restoration. 5\. State-changing model-management actions are recorded in the audit trail.  |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Responses** |
| 1\. The System Administrator selects **Model Management**.  | 2\. The system displays the active model, training date, training-data period, evaluation results and available model versions. **(Requirement: FR-DP-12)**  |
|  | 3\. The system provides options to retrain the model, review evaluation results, activate a candidate model or restore a previous valid model. **(Requirement: FR-DP-09, FR-DP-12)**  |
| 4\. The Administrator selects a model-management action.  | 5\. The system validates the prerequisites and permissions required for the selected action. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04)**  |
|  | 6\. The system performs the appropriate model-management subflow. **(Requirement: FR-DP-09, FR-DP-12)**   |
|  | 7\. For an action that changes the active model, the system requests confirmation before applying the change. **(Requirement: FR-DP-12)**  |
| 8\. The Administrator confirms the action where required.  | 9\. The system stores the resulting model information and records the state-changing action in the audit trail. **(Requirement: FR-DP-12, NFR-DAT-03)**  |
|  | 10\. The system displays the updated model status and outcome. **(Requirement: FR-DP-12)**  |
| 11\. The Administrator reviews the outcome.  |  |
| **Alternative Flows and Subflows A1. Step 4 – Retrain the prediction model** The Administrator selects the **Retrain Model**. The system verifies that at least 30 distinct valid daily records per bread category are available. **(Requirement: FR-DP-09)** The system identifies each sales record as actual, imported historical or simulation-generated. **(Requirement: FR-DP-01, NFR-ACC-07)** The system uses daily units sold as the target variable and prepares the required historical, temporal, weather and holiday features. **(Requirement: FR-DP-09)** The system partitions the data chronologically into training, validation and later test datasets. The test dataset is not used for model training or model-parameter selection. **(Requirement: NFR-ACC-01)** The system trains a new Random Forest candidate model and a Linear Regression baseline using the corresponding datasets. **(Requirement: FR-DP-10)** The system calculates MAE and RMSE using all test observations and calculates MAPE only where actual units sold are greater than zero. If all test observations have zero actual sales, MAPE is reported as unavailable. **(Requirement: FR-DP-11, NFR-ACC-02)** The system also calculates R² and compares the Random Forest candidate with the Linear Regression baseline using the same datasets. **(Requirement: FR-DP-10, FR-DP-11)** The system stores the successfully trained model as an inactive candidate version with its training date, data period, configuration and evaluation results. **(Requirement: FR-DP-12)** The system displays the candidate model and its performance comparison. The active model remains unchanged. **(Requirement: FR-DP-12)** **A2. Step 4 – Review model-evaluation results** The Administrator selects a model version. The system displays its training date, data period, data-source composition, evaluation metrics, model configuration and comparison results. Evaluation results obtained from simulation-generated records are clearly identified as simulation-based performance. **(Requirement: FR-DP-11, NFR-ACC-07) A3. Step 4 – Activate a candidate model** The Administrator selects a valid candidate model. The system displays its evaluation results and compares them with the active model using the same evaluation criteria. If the candidate satisfies the activation rules, the Administrator confirms the activation. The system marks the candidate as active and retains the previous model as a restorable version. **(Requirement: FR-DP-12) A4. Step 4 – Restore a previous valid model** The Administrator selects a previous valid model version. The system displays its model information and requests confirmation. After confirmation, the system activates the selected version and retains the replaced model in the version history. **(Requirement: FR-DP-12) A5. Subflow A1 – Insufficient or invalid historical data** If fewer than 30 distinct valid daily records per bread category remain after validation, the system prevents retraining and displays the number of available records, the minimum requirement and identified data-quality problems. The active model remains unchanged. **(Requirement: FR-DP-09) A6. Subflow A1 – Model training or evaluation failure** If model training, evaluation or candidate-model storage fails, the system records the error, does not create an incomplete valid model version and preserves the current active model. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-02) A7. Subflow A3 – Candidate model performs worse** If the candidate model’s primary MAE is worse than that of the active model on the same chronological test dataset, the system prevents it from replacing the active model and explains the performance difference. The candidate results may remain stored for review. **(Requirement: NFR-ACC-05) A8. Subflows A3–A4 – Activation or restoration failure** If activation or restoration fails, the system rolls back the incomplete change, preserves the previously active model and displays an error message. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-02)** |  |

*Table 3.13: Use Case Specification for Manage Inventory and Product Data* 

| Use Case ID:  UC-INV-01   |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Use Case Name:** Manage Inventory and Product Data  |  |
| **Actor:** System Administrator   |  |
| **Supporting Actors:** – |  |
| **Brief Description:** The System Administrator manages ingredients, bread categories, recipes and inventory batches required by the prediction, production-recommendation and POS-simulation modules. The Administrator can also review inventory movements and inventory-quality issues.  |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. The System Administrator is logged in. 2\. The Administrator has permission to manage inventory and product data. 3\. The required database and inventory configurations are available.   |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. Valid changes to ingredients, bread categories, recipes or inventory batches are stored. 2\. Inventory quantities and quality statuses are recalculated where applicable. 3\. Restocking activities create corresponding inventory-movement records. 4\. Updated data become available to production recommendations and POS simulations. 5\. State-changing operations are recorded in the audit trail. |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Responses** |
| 1\. The System Administrator selects **Inventory and Product Management**.  | 2\. The system displays the available management categories: Ingredients, Bread Categories, Recipes, Inventory Batches, Inventory Movements and Quality Issues. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01, FR-INV-02, FR-INV-03, FR-INV-04)**  |
| 3\. The Administrator selects a management category.   | 4\. The system retrieves and displays the corresponding records and their current statuses. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01, FR-INV-02)**  |
| 5\. The Administrator selects a permitted management action.  | 6\. The system displays the appropriate form, information or inventory records for the selected action. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01, FR-INV-02)**  |
| 7\. The Administrator enters or updates the required information.  | 8\. The system validates required fields, quantities, measurement units, dates and relationships. **(Requirement: NFR-DAT-01)**  |
| 9\. The Administrator confirms the operation.  | 10\. The system stores the valid changes and performs the corresponding inventory or product-data subflow. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01, FR-INV-02, FR-INV-03)**  |
|  | 11\. Where inventory information is affected, the system recalculates the available quantity, reorder status, expiry status and relevant quality indicators. **(Requirement: FR-INV-04, FR-INV-05)**  |
|  | 12\. The system records the state-changing operation in the audit trail. **(Requirement: NFR-DAT-03)**  |
|  | 13\. The system displays a success message and the updated information.   |
| 14\. The Administrator reviews the updated information.  |  |
| **Alternative Flows and Subflows A1. Step 5 – Manage ingredients** The Administrator creates or updates an ingredient by providing its name, measurement unit, reorder threshold and active status. The system validates and stores the ingredient information. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01)** If an ingredient is no longer required, the Administrator may deactivate it. An ingredient referenced by existing recipes, inventory batches or transaction records shall not be permanently deleted. **(Requirement: NFR-DAT-01) A2. Step 5 – Manage bread categories** The Administrator creates or updates a bread category by providing its name, selling price, description and active status. The system validates and stores the bread-category information. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01)** A bread category referenced by predictions, production decisions, simulations or historical records shall not be permanently deleted. **A3. Step 5 – Manage recipes** The Administrator selects a bread category and defines the ingredients and quantities required to produce one unit. The system validates that every selected ingredient is active, each quantity is greater than zero and no ingredient is duplicated within the same recipe. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01, NFR-DAT-01)** The system stores the valid recipe and makes it available for ingredient-requirement and maximum-producible-quantity calculations. **(Requirement: FR-INV-07) A4. Step 5 – Restock an inventory batch** The Administrator selects an active ingredient and chooses **Restock Inventory**. The system displays the ingredient’s measurement unit, available quantity and existing batches. The Administrator enters the received quantity, unit cost, received date, expiry date and optional supplier information. The system validates that the quantity is positive, the unit cost is non-negative and the expiry date is later than the received date. **(Requirement: FR-INV-02, NFR-DAT-01)** The system creates a separate inventory batch and updates the ingredient’s available quantity. **(Requirement: FR-INV-02)** The system creates a corresponding restocking inventory-movement record. **(Requirement: FR-INV-03)** The system recalculates the ingredient’s low-stock and expiry statuses. **(Requirement: FR-INV-04)**  **A5. Step 5 – View inventory movements** The Administrator selects **Inventory Movements**. The system displays restocking and consumption movements, including the affected ingredient, quantity, movement type, related batch, date and related production decision where applicable. **(Requirement: FR-INV-03)** This is a read-only operation and does not modify the original inventory records. **A6. Step 5 – Review inventory-quality issues** The Administrator selects **Quality Issues**. The system identifies and displays low-stock ingredients, expired or soon-to-expire batches, incomplete recipes and inventory inconsistencies. **(Requirement: FR-INV-04)** Expired batches are excluded from the valid available quantity used for production-feasibility calculations. **(Requirement: FR-INV-05) A7. Step 8 – Invalid or incomplete information** If a required value is missing or invalid, the system identifies the affected field and prevents the record from being stored until the information is corrected. **(Requirement: NFR-DAT-01)** Examples include: A zero or negative inventory quantity An invalid measurement unit A negative unit cost An expiry date earlier than the received date An incomplete recipe A duplicated ingredient in the same recipe **A8. Step 9 – Administrator cancels the operation** If the Administrator cancels before confirmation, the system returns to the relevant management screen without storing any changes. **A9. Steps 10–12 – Storage or inventory-update failure** If a database or processing error occurs, the system rolls back the incomplete operation. It shall not create a partial batch, product-data update, inventory-movement record or audit record. The existing data remain unchanged, and the Administrator may retry. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01)** |  |

*Table 3.14: Use Case Specification for Generate Production Recommendation*  

| Use Case ID:  UC-INV-02 |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Use Case Name:** Generate Production Recommendation   |  |
| **Actor:** Bakery Manager    |  |
| **Supporting Actors:** – |  |
| **Brief Description:** The Bakery Manager generates inventory-aware production recommendations based on the next-day sales prediction, bread-category recipes, valid ingredient inventory and configured operational constraints. The system calculates production feasibility, identifies ingredient shortages and recommends feasible production quantities.  |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. The Bakery Manager is logged in. 2\. A valid next-day sales prediction exists. 3\. At least one active bread category exists. 4\. The applicable bread categories have complete recipe information. 5\. Ingredient inventory records are available and valid.   |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. A production recommendation is generated for each applicable bread category. 2\. The recommended quantities, maximum producible quantities, limiting ingredients and ingredient shortages are available for review. 3\. The recommendations are available for production-decision confirmation. Their snapshots are stored only when the Bakery Manager confirms the corresponding production decisions. 4\. No ingredient inventory is deducted during production recommendation generation. |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Responses** |
| 1\. The Bakery Manager selects **Production Recommendation**.     | 2\. The system displays the available next-day sales prediction and its prediction date.   |
| 3\. The Bakery Manager selects **Generate Recommendation**.  | 4\. The system validates the prediction, active bread categories, recipes, inventory records and applicable operational parameters. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01, FR-INV-08)**    |
|  | 5\. The system retrieves the predicted sales quantity and recipe requirements for each applicable bread category. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01, FR-INV-08)**  |
|  | 6\. The system calculates the ingredients required to satisfy the predicted sales quantities. **(Requirement: FR-INV-07)**  |
|  | 7\. The system calculates the available ingredient quantities from valid, unexpired inventory batches. **(Requirement: FR-INV-05)**  |
|  | 8\. The system accounts for confirmed but unprocessed production commitments for the selected date and calculates recommendations using a temporary ingredient balance. Unconfirmed categories are processed in display order, with each proposed allocation reducing the balance available to subsequent categories. The combined ingredient requirements must remain within valid available inventory and applicable operational constraints. No stored inventory quantities are changed.  **(Requirement: FR-INV-07, FR-INV-08)**  |
|  | 9\. The system identifies limiting ingredients and calculates any ingredient shortages. **(Requirement: FR-INV-09)**   |
|  | 10\. The system generates and displays a feasible recommended production quantity for each bread category. **(Requirement: FR-INV-08)**  |
|  | 11\. Where the predicted quantity is not feasible, the system presents reduced-production or ingredient-restocking options. **(Requirement: FR-INV-09)**  |
|  | 12\. The system displays the predicted sales quantity, maximum producible quantity, recommended production quantity, limiting ingredients and available options. **(Requirement: FR-INV-08, FR-INV-09)**  |
| 13\. The Bakery Manager reviews the recommendations and identifies shortages.  |  |
| **Alternative Flows of Events A1. Step 4 – No valid prediction is available**If no valid next-day sales prediction exists, the system prevents recommendation generation and instructs the Bakery Manager to generate a prediction first. **(Requirement: FR-INV-08) A2. Step 4 – Missing or incomplete recipe information**If an active bread category does not have a complete recipe, the system identifies the category as an inventory-quality issue and does not generate a recommendation for that category. **(Requirement: FR-INV-01, NFR-DAT-01) A3. Step 7 – Expired ingredient batches are detected**If expired batches exist, the system excludes them from the valid available inventory and identifies them as inventory-quality issues. **(Requirement: FR-INV-04, FR-INV-05) A4. Steps 8–11 – Insufficient ingredients**If the available valid ingredients cannot satisfy the predicted sales quantity, the system calculates a reduced feasible production quantity, identifies the limiting ingredients and displays the quantities that should be restocked. **(Requirement: FR-INV-09) A5. Steps 8–11 – Production is not feasible**If an essential ingredient is unavailable or an operational constraint prevents production, the system recommends a production quantity of zero and explains the reason. **(Requirement: FR-INV-07, FR-INV-09) A6. Step 4 – Inventory inconsistency is detected**If the stored inventory total differs from the quantities calculated from valid inventory batches, the system identifies the inconsistency and prevents the affected inventory from being used until the issue is reviewed. **(Requirement: NFR-DAT-01) A7. Steps 8–10 – Recommendation generation fails**If a processing or database error occurs, the system displays an error message and does not return an incomplete production recommendation. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01)** |  |

*Table 3.15: Use Case Specification for Confirm Production Decision*

| Use Case ID:  UC-INV-03 |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Use Case Name:** Confirm Production Decision  |  |
| **Actor:** Bakery Manager    |  |
| **Supporting Actors:** – |  |
| **Brief Description:** The Bakery Manager reviews the generated production recommendation and confirms the final quantity of each bread category to be produced. The Manager may accept, reduce or override the recommended quantity, subject to production-feasibility constraints.  |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. The Bakery Manager is logged in. 2\. A production recommendation exists for the selected production date. 3\. The required recipes and current inventory information are available. 4\. The maximum producible quantity has been calculated for each applicable bread category. |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. The confirmed production decision is stored with its production date, final quantity, decision type, reason, time and Manager information. 2\. A reason is stored when the Manager reduces or overrides the recommendation. 3\. The confirmed production decision becomes available to the POS Simulation module. 4\. An audit record of the production decision is created. 5\. Ingredient inventory is not deducted merely by confirming the production decision.  |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Responses** |
| 1\. The bakery manager selects **Production Recommendation**.  | 2\. The system displays the latest production recommendation for the selected production date.  |
| 3\. The bakery manager selects a bread category.  | 4\. The system displays its predicted sales quantity, recommended production quantity, maximum producible quantity, required ingredients and identified shortages. **(Requirement: FR-INV-08, FR-INV-09)**  |
| 5\. The Bakery Manager selects **Accept**, **Reduce** or **Override**.  | 6\. If Accept is selected, the system uses the recommended quantity. If Reduce or Override is selected, the system displays a field for the adjusted quantity and reason. **(Requirement: FR-INV-10, FR-INV-11)**  |
| 7\. Where required, the Bakery Manager enters the adjusted quantity and reason.  | 8\. The system validates that the proposed quantity is a non-negative whole number and includes a reason when the recommendation is changed. It recalculates production feasibility using the proposed quantity and all other confirmed but unprocessed decisions for the selected date. If an existing decision is being revised, its previous quantity is excluded. Confirmation is permitted only when the combined ingredient requirements remain within valid available inventory and applicable operational constraints. **(Requirement: FR-INV-11)**   |
| 9\. The Bakery Manager selects **Confirm Production Decision**.   | 10\. The system displays a confirmation summary containing the predicted sales quantity, recommended quantity, final quantity and decision type. **(Requirement: FR-INV-07, FR-INV-11)**  |
| 11\. The Bakery Manager confirms the information.  | 12\. The system serialises production confirmations for the same date and rechecks the combined ingredient requirements before saving. If the plan remains feasible, it stores the final quantity, decision type, reason, production date, confirmation time and Manager identifier in the same transaction. Stored inventory quantities remain unchanged. Recommendations affected by the confirmed change are recalculated before further confirmation. **(Requirement: FR-INV-11, FR-INV-12, NFR-REL-01)**  |
|  | 13\. The system creates an audit record and makes the confirmed decision available to the POS Simulation module. **(Requirement: FR-INV-12, NFR-DAT-03)**  |
|  | 14\. The system displays a successful confirmation message.  |
| 15\. The Bakery Manager repeats the process for other applicable bread categories where required.  |  |
| **Alternative Flows of Events A1. Step 2 – No valid production recommendation** If no valid production recommendation exists for the selected date, the system prevents confirmation and prompts the Bakery Manager to generate a recommendation first. **(Requirement: FR-INV-08) A2. Steps 8 and 12 – Invalid or infeasible production quantity**  If the proposed quantity is negative, contains a decimal value, violates an operational constraint or causes the combined ingredient requirements to exceed valid available inventory, the system rejects the confirmation and displays the limiting ingredients and shortages. The existing confirmed decisions remain unchanged. The Bakery Manager must revise the proposed quantity or other unprocessed production decisions, or request the System Administrator to restock the required ingredients, before retrying. **(Requirement: FR-INV-07, FR-INV-11) A3. Step 8 – Adjustment reason is missing** If the Bakery Manager reduces or overrides the recommended quantity without providing a reason, the system requests a reason before allowing confirmation. **(Requirement: FR-INV-11) A4. Steps 9–11 – Manager cancels the confirmation** If the Bakery Manager cancels before final confirmation, the system returns to the recommendation screen without storing a new production decision. **A5. Steps 12–13 – Production decision cannot be stored** If a processing, database or network error occurs, the system does not create an incomplete production decision or audit record. The previous data remain unchanged, and the Manager may retry. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01)** |  |

*Table 3.16: Use Case Specification for Run POS Simulation* 

| Use Case ID:  UC-POS-01  |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Use Case Name:** Run POS Simulation  |  |
| **Actor:** Bakery Manager    |  |
| **Supporting Actors:** Weather Service, Calendar/Holiday Service  |  |
| **Brief Description:** The Bakery Manager manually initiates a POS simulation for a selected production date. The system uses the stored sales prediction as the baseline and applies configured time-slot and stochastic variations, together with the selected date’s contextual information, to simulate customer purchases. It calculates units sold, lost sales, estimated demand, revenue and leftovers based on the confirmed production quantities.  |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. The Bakery Manager is logged in. 2\. A production decision has been confirmed for the selected simulation date. 3\. At least one active bread category has a confirmed production quantity. 4\. Product prices and simulation parameters are configured. 5\. The required external-service configurations are available. 6\. The confirmed production decision has not been used for another completed POS simulation. |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. The completed simulation and simulated transactions are stored. 2\. Units sold, lost sales, estimated demand, revenue and leftovers are calculated. 3\. The resulting sales records are identified as simulation-generated. 4\. The results become available for dashboards, reports and leftover management. 5\. Required ingredients are deducted through FIFO exactly once, and the related inventory movements are recorded. |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Responses** |
| 1\. The Bakery Manager selects **POS Simulation**. | 2\. The system displays the simulation screen, uses the current date by default and shows dates with confirmed production decisions. **(Requirement: FR-POS-01, FR-POS-02)** |
| 3\. The Bakery Manager selects a production date. | 4\. The system retrieves the confirmed production decision and stored sales prediction for that date. **(Requirement: FR-POS-02)** |
|  | 5\. The system displays the confirmed production quantities for each bread category. |
| 6\. The Bakery Manager selects **Run Simulation**. | 7\. The system validates the production decision, stored prediction, product prices, simulation parameters and previous simulation status. **(Requirement: FR-POS-01, FR-POS-02)** |
|  | 8\. The system verifies that sufficient valid ingredient inventory is available for the confirmed production quantities. **(Requirement: FR-POS-08)** |
|  | 9\. The system deducts the required ingredients from the oldest valid inventory batches using FIFO. **(Requirement: FR-INV-05, FR-INV-06, FR-POS-08)** |
|  | 10\. The system creates inventory-movement records linked to the confirmed production decision and marks its inventory as processed. **(Requirement: FR-INV-03, FR-POS-08)** |
|  | 11\. The system retrieves weather and public-holiday information for the selected simulation date and derives the applicable temporal information. **(Requirement: FR-POS-03)** |
|  | 12\. The system uses the stored sales prediction as the baseline and applies configured time-slot and stochastic variations to generate simulated customer demand. Contextual factors already represented in the stored prediction shall not be applied twice. **(Requirement: FR-POS-03, FR-POS-04)** |
|  | 13\. The system processes simulated customer purchases without allowing units sold to exceed the confirmed production quantity. **(Requirement: FR-POS-04)** |
|  | 14\. The system records the bread category, quantity sold, unit price, subtotal and transaction time for each simulated purchase. **(Requirement: FR-POS-07)** |
|  | 15\. When simulated demand exceeds the remaining quantity, the system records the unmet quantity as lost sales. **(Requirement: FR-POS-05)** |
|  | 16\. The system calculates estimated demand as units sold plus lost sales. **(Requirement: FR-POS-06)** |
|  | 17\. The system calculates leftovers as the confirmed production quantity minus units sold and calculates simulated revenue. **(Requirement: FR-POS-06)** |
|  | 18\. The system stores the completed results and identifies all generated sales records as simulation-generated. **(Requirement: FR-POS-07)** |
|  | 19\. The system makes the results available for dashboards, reports and leftover management. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-01, FR-RPT-01)** |
|  | 20\. The system displays the production quantity, units sold, lost sales, estimated demand, revenue and leftovers for every bread category. **(Requirement: FR-POS-07)** |
| 21\. The Bakery Manager reviews the results. |  |
| **Alternative Flows of Events A1. Step 4 – No confirmed production decision** If no confirmed production decision exists for the selected date, the system prevents the simulation from starting and prompts the Bakery Manager to confirm a production decision first. **(Requirement: FR-POS-02) A2. Steps 4 and 7 – Stored sales prediction is unavailable** If no stored sales prediction exists for the selected date, the system prevents the simulation from starting and prompts the Bakery Manager to generate the required prediction. **(Requirement: FR-DP-05) A3. Step 7 – Simulation configuration is invalid** If product prices, bread categories or simulation parameters are missing or invalid, the system identifies the missing configuration and prevents the simulation from starting. **(Requirement: NFR-DAT-01) A4. Step 7 – A completed simulation already exists** If the confirmed production decision has already been used for a completed simulation, the system prevents another simulation from being created to avoid duplicate sales records and ingredient deductions. **(Requirement: FR-POS-08) A5. Step 8 – Insufficient valid ingredient inventory** If sufficient valid ingredients are unavailable, the system prevents the simulation from starting and displays the identified shortages. The Bakery Manager must restock the ingredients or revise the production decision. **(Requirement: FR-POS-08) A6. Steps 9–10 – Inventory deduction fails** If ingredient deduction or inventory-movement recording fails, the system cancels the simulation initiation and rolls back incomplete inventory changes. The production decision remains unprocessed. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01) A7. Step 11 – External contextual data are unavailable** If weather or public-holiday information cannot be retrieved, the system displays an error and allows a retry. Where permitted, it may continue using marked default or recently available information. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-03) A8. Steps 13–15 – Simulated demand exceeds available products** The system sells only the remaining available quantity and records the unmet demand as lost sales. Product availability shall not become negative. If the confirmed quantity is zero, all simulated demand for that category is recorded as lost sales. **(Requirement: FR-POS-04, FR-POS-05, NFR-REL-04) A9. Steps 16–19 – No leftovers remain** If all produced units of a bread category are sold, the system records zero leftovers, and no donation or waste recommendation is required for that category. **(Requirement: FR-POS-06) A10. Steps 13–18 – Simulation processing or storage fails** If simulation processing or storage fails before the transaction is committed, the system rolls back all database changes made by that attempt, including ingredient deductions, inventory movements, sales transactions, daily results and simulation-generated sales-history records. The confirmed production decision remains unprocessed and available for retry. The system displays an error message and allows the Bakery Manager to retry. On retry, ingredient availability is revalidated and FIFO deduction is performed again because the failed attempt retained no deductions. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01, FR-POS-08)**  |  |

*Table 3.17: Use Case Specification for Manage Leftovers, Donations and Waste* 

| Use Case ID:  UC-LDW-01   |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Use Case Name:** Manage Leftovers, Donations and Waste  |  |
| **Actor:** Bakery Manager    |  |
| **Supporting Actors:** – |  |
| **Brief Description:** The Bakery Manager reviews leftovers calculated from a completed POS simulation and records how the available leftovers are handled. The system recommends donation or waste according to configured rules, while the Manager records the selected action and updates donation statuses where applicable.    |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. The Bakery Manager is logged in. |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. The selected donation or waste action is stored. 2\. A donation record is linked to an active charity partner. 3\. A waste record contains its quantity and disposal reason. 4\. The remaining unallocated leftover quantity is updated. 5\. Donation statuses are stored and may subsequently be updated. 6\. The resulting information becomes available for dashboards and reports. 7\. State-changing operations are recorded in the audit trail. |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Responses** |
| 1\. The Bakery Manager selects **Leftover Management**. | 2\. The system displays completed simulation dates and their leftover summaries. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-01)** |
| 3\. The Bakery Manager selects a simulation date and bread category. | 4\. The system retrieves the calculated leftover and remaining unallocated quantity. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-01)** |
|  | 5\. The system displays the produced quantity, units sold, calculated leftovers and previously allocated quantities. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-01)** |
|  | 6\. The system evaluates the available leftovers using the configured leftover-handling rules and displays a recommended donation or waste action. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-02)** |
| 7\. The Bakery Manager reviews the recommendation and selects **Record Donation** or **Record Waste**. | 8\. The system displays the appropriate form for the selected action. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-03, FR-LDW-04)** |
| 9\. The Bakery Manager enters the allocation quantity and the required donation or waste information. | 10\. The system validates that the quantity is greater than zero and does not exceed the remaining unallocated leftover quantity. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-05)** |
|  | 11\. For a donation, the system validates the selected charity partner. For waste, the system validates that a disposal reason is provided. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-03, FR-LDW-04)** |
| 12\. The Bakery Manager confirms the action. | 13\. The system creates the donation or waste record. For a donation, the system assigns the configured initial status, such as Pending. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-03, FR-LDW-04, FR-LDW-06)** |
|  | 14\. The system deducts the allocated quantity from the remaining unallocated leftover quantity. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-05, FR-LDW-06)** |
|  | 15\. The system records the action in the audit trail and displays the updated leftover summary. **(Requirement: NFR-DAT-03)** |
| 16\. The Bakery Manager repeats the process if unallocated leftovers remain. |  |
| **Alternative Flows and Subflows A1. Step 4 – No completed POS simulation** If no completed POS simulation exists for the selected date, the system informs the Bakery Manager that leftover information is unavailable and prevents a donation or waste record from being created. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-01) A2. Steps 4–5 – No leftovers are available** If all produced units were sold, the system displays a leftover quantity of zero. No donation or waste action is required. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-01) A3. Step 6 – A recommendation cannot be generated** If the required product information or leftover-handling rule is unavailable, the system informs the Bakery Manager that no recommendation can be generated. The Manager may select an action manually if permitted. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-02) A4. Step 10 – Invalid allocation quantity** If the quantity is zero, negative or greater than the remaining unallocated leftover quantity, the system rejects it and requests a valid quantity. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-05, NFR-REL-04) A5. Step 11 – No valid charity partner is selected** If no active charity partner is available or selected, the system prevents the donation from being confirmed. The Bakery Manager may leave the quantity unallocated or record another permitted action. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-03) A6. Step 11 – Waste reason is missing** If the Bakery Manager attempts to record waste without a disposal reason, the system requests a reason before allowing confirmation. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-04) A7. Step 7 – Update donation status** The Bakery Manager selects an existing donation record and chooses **Update Status**. The system displays the permitted statuses. After the Manager confirms a valid status, the system stores the updated status and update time. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-06) A8. Step 12 – Manager cancels the action** If the Bakery Manager cancels before confirmation, the system does not create a donation or waste record, and the leftover quantity remains unchanged. **A9. Steps 13–15 – Record storage or leftover update fails** If a processing, database or network error occurs, the system rolls back the incomplete operation. It does not create a partial donation or waste record or change the remaining leftover quantity. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01)** |  |

| Use Case ID:  UC-RPT-01    |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Use Case Name:** View Dashboards and Reports  |  |
| **Actor:** Bakery Manager, System Administrator     |  |

| **Brief Description:** An authorised user views role-appropriate dashboards and reports containing prediction, production, inventory, simulated sales, lost-sales, revenue, leftover, donation and waste information. The user may filter the displayed information, generate a weekly report, inspect detailed records and export supported reports.   |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. The user is logged in. 2\. The user has permission to access the selected dashboard or report.   |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. The requested dashboard or report is displayed. 2\. A generated weekly report may be stored with its reporting period, generation time and generating user. 3\. An exported report is generated in the selected supported format. 4\. Original operational and simulation records remain unchanged.  |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Responses** |
| 1\. The user selects **Dashboard and Reports**. | 2\. The system identifies the user’s role and displays the dashboards and report types permitted for that role. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04, FR-RPT-01)** |
|  | 3\. The system displays summary information for predictions, production decisions, simulated sales, lost sales, revenue, leftovers, donations and waste. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-01)** |
| 4\. The user selects a dashboard, report type or reporting action. | 5\. The system displays the available date, reporting-period and bread-category filters. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-02)** |

|  | 10\. The system groups and aggregates the records according to the selected date, reporting period and bread category. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-02)** |
|  | 11\. The system calculates the applicable totals, averages and performance indicators. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-05)** |
|  | 12\. The system identifies information derived from POS simulations as simulation-generated. **(Requirement: FR-POS-07, NFR-ACC-07)** |
|  | 13\. The system displays the requested dashboard or report using summaries, tables and charts. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-01)** |
| 14\. The user reviews the displayed information. | 15\. The system provides permitted options to view detailed records, modify filters, generate a weekly report or export the report. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-02, FR-RPT-03, FR-RPT-06)** |

The system displays role-appropriate summary cards, charts and indicators based on the selected reporting period. The displayed information may include: Predicted sales Confirmed production quantities Units sold and lost sales Simulated revenue Leftovers, donations and waste Low-stock and expiry information **(Requirement: FR-RPT-01, FR-RPT-02) A2. Step 4 – Generate weekly report** The user selects **Weekly Report**. The system displays the weekly-report form with the current week selected by default. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-03)** The user selects or confirms a seven-consecutive-day reporting period. The system retrieves the relevant predictions, production decisions, simulation results, leftovers, donations and waste records. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-03)** The system groups the records by date and bread category. The system calculates total and average units sold, lost sales, estimated demand, production quantity, revenue, leftovers, donations and waste. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-03, FR-RPT-05)** The system compares predicted sales with corresponding stored daily units sold. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-04)** The system calculates sales-fulfilment, leftover and waste rates. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-05)** The system generates and displays the weekly report. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-03)**  **A3. Step 15 – View detailed records** The user selects an item, chart or summary value. The system displays the corresponding permitted records, filtered by date, reporting period or bread category. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-02) A4. Step 15 – Export report** The user selects the **Export Report**. The system displays the supported export formats, such as PDF and CSV. The user selects a format. The system generates the exported report using the currently selected filters without modifying the original records. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-06)** The system makes the generated file available to the user. **Exception flows**  **A5. Step 2 – User is not authorised** If the user does not have permission to access the selected dashboard or report, the system denies access and displays an appropriate message. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04) A6. Step 7 – Invalid reporting period** If the end date is earlier than the start date or the weekly period does not contain seven consecutive days, the system requests a valid reporting period. **(Requirement: NFR-DAT-01) A7. Step 9 – No matching records are available** If no records match the selected criteria, the system displays a no-data message instead of generating an empty or misleading report. **A8. Steps 9–13 – Some daily records are missing** If records are available for only part of the selected period, the system may generate a partial report but shall clearly identify the dates or categories with missing information. **A9. Subflow A2 – No corresponding prediction exists** If a daily sales record has no corresponding prediction, the system excludes that record from prediction-error comparison while retaining it in other applicable report calculations. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-04) A10. Subflow A2 – Division by zero** If the denominator required for a fulfilment, leftover or waste rate is zero, the system displays the corresponding rate as **Not Applicable** instead of performing division by zero. **(Requirement: FR-RPT-05) A11. Steps 9–13 – Report generation fails** If report generation fails, the system displays an error message and does not store an incomplete report. The original operational records remain unchanged. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01) A12. Subflow A4 – Export fails** If the report cannot be exported, the system displays an error message while retaining the displayed report and its underlying records. The user may retry or select another supported format. |  |

Bakery Managers receive operational notifications, while System Administrators receive relevant administrative and system notifications.    |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. The user is logged in. 2\. The user account is active. 3\. The user has permission to access notifications. 4\. The notification function is available.   |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. The relevant notifications are displayed according to the user’s role. 2\. The read status of a selected notification is updated where requested. 3\. The original operational or administrative record associated with the notification remains unchanged.   |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Responses** |
| 1\. The user selects **Notifications**. | 2\. The system identifies the authenticated user and assigned role. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04)** |
|  | 3\. The system retrieves notifications that the user is authorised to view. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-02)** |
|  | 4\. The system displays the notifications according to date, category and read status, with the newest notification shown first. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-02)** |
| 5\. The user selects a notification. | 6\. The system displays the notification category, message, creation date, read status and related record information where available. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-02)** |
|  | 7\. If the notification is unread, the system provides an option to mark it as read. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-03)** |
| 8\. The user selects **Mark as Read**. | 9\. The system updates the selected notification’s status and records the time it was marked as read. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-03)** |
|  | 10\. The system displays the updated notification status. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-03)** |
| 11\. The user continues reviewing notifications or returns to the previous screen. |  |
| **Alternative Flows and Subflows  A1. Step 3 – Bakery Manager views operational notifications** The system displays operational notifications relevant to the Bakery Manager, which may include: Low ingredient stock Low prediction confidence Lost sales Excessive leftovers Donation-related information Relevant operation failures **(Requirement: FR-ALT-01, FR-ALT-02) A2. Step 3 – System Administrator views administrative notifications** The system displays administrative notifications relevant to the System Administrator, which may include: Inventory-quality issues Model-training or model-evaluation failures External-service failures System or configuration problems User-management or administrative events **(Requirement: FR-ALT-01, FR-ALT-02) A3. Step 4 – User filters notifications** The user selects a notification category, date range or read status. The system validates the filter and displays matching notifications that the user is authorised to view. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-02) A4. Step 3 – No notifications are available** If the user has no relevant notifications, the system displays a no-notifications message instead of an empty or misleading notification list. **A5. Step 3 – User is not authorised to view a notification** If a notification is not associated with the user’s role or permissions, the system prevents access to that notification and its related information. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04, FR-ALT-02) A6. Step 6 – Related record is unavailable** If the operational or administrative record associated with a notification is unavailable, the system still displays the notification message but informs the user that the related record cannot be opened. **A7. Steps 8–9 – Notification is already marked as read** If the selected notification has already been marked as read, the system retains the existing read status and does not create a duplicate update. **A8. Step 9 – Read-status update fails** If a database or network error prevents the read status from being updated, the system retains the previous status, displays an error message and allows the user to retry. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01) A9. Steps 1–10 – Session has expired** If the authenticated session expires, the system prevents further notification access and returns the user to the login screen. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-01, FR-UAM-04)** |  |

*Table 3.20: Use Case Specification for Deliver Background Notification* 

| Use Case ID:  UC-ALT-02     |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Use Case Name:** Deliver Background Notification  |  |
| **Actor:** – |  |
| **Supporting Actors:** Push Notification Service  |  |
| **Trigger:** An eligible system event creates a notification that may require background delivery.  |  |
| **Brief Description:** When an eligible notification event occurs, the system stores an in-application notification and sends an appropriate background-notification request to the configured Push Notification Service. The service attempts to deliver the notification to the registered device of the relevant user.  |  |
| **Preconditions:**  1\. An eligible notification event has occurred. 2\. The intended recipient and notification category have been identified. 3\. The Push Notification Service is configured.  |  |
| **Postconditions** 1\. The in-application notification is stored. 2\. A background-delivery request is submitted where the delivery requirements are satisfied. 3\. The notification-delivery status is recorded as submitted, delivered, failed or skipped where supported. 4\. Failure to deliver the background notification does not remove the in-application notification.   |  |
| **Main Flow of the Events:** |  |
| **Trigger or External-Service Action** | **System Response** |
| 1\. An eligible system event occurs, such as low stock, low prediction confidence, lost sales, excessive leftovers or an operation failure. | 2\. The system determines the notification category, message and intended recipient. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-01)** |
|  | 3\. The system verifies that the intended recipient is authorised to receive the notification. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04)** |
|  | 4\. The system stores the notification as an unread in-application notification. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-01, FR-ALT-02)** |
|  | 5\. The system checks the user’s notification preference and registered device token. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-04)** |
|  | 6\. The system prepares a background-notification request containing the permitted notification summary and target-device information. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-04)** |
|  | 7\. The system securely submits the request to the configured Push Notification Service. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-04, NFR-SEC-04)** |
| 8\. The Push Notification Service accepts the request and attempts to deliver it to the registered device. | 9\. The system receives or retrieves the available delivery response from the Push Notification Service. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-04)** |
|  | 10\. The system records the background-delivery status and relevant response information. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-04)** |
|  | 11\. The system retains the corresponding notification in the notification centre for later viewing. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-02)**  |
| **Alternative Flows of Events A1. Step 5 – Background notifications are disabled** If the user has disabled background notifications, the system does not submit a push notification request. It retains the in-application notification and records the background-delivery status as skipped. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-02, FR-ALT-04) A2. Step 5 – No valid device token is available** If the user has no valid registered device token, the system does not submit the delivery request. It retains the in-application notification and records the push delivery as unavailable or failed. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-04) A3. Step 3 – No authorised recipient can be identified** If the system cannot identify an authorised recipient, it does not send the background notification. The event and failure reason are recorded for administrative review. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04) A4. Step 4 – In-application notification cannot be stored** If the notification record cannot be stored, the system cancels the background-delivery operation to avoid delivering a notification without a corresponding system record. The error is recorded. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01) A5. Steps 7–9 – Push Notification Service is unavailable** If the Push Notification Service is unavailable, the system retains the in-application notification, records the background-delivery attempt as failed and allows the delivery to be retried where supported. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-03) A6. Steps 8–10 – Delivery request is rejected** If the Push Notification Service rejects the request because of an invalid token, invalid payload or configuration problem, the system records the failure reason. The in-application notification remains available. **(Requirement: FR-ALT-04) A7. Step 6 – Notification contains restricted information** The background-notification payload shall contain only a permitted summary and shall not expose sensitive account, inventory or administrative information. The user must authenticate before opening protected details in the application. **(Requirement: NFR-SEC-01, NFR-SEC-04)** |  |

| **Alternative Flows and Subflows A1. Step 4 – Manage users and roles** The Administrator selects **Users and Roles**. The system validates the account information and selected role. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-05, NFR-DAT-01)** The system stores the valid changes and applies the updated permissions to subsequent authenticated access. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04, FR-UAM-05)** A user account referenced by existing operational or audit records shall be deactivated rather than permanently deleted. **A2. Step 4 – Manage bakery settings** The Administrator updates permitted bakery information, such as the bakery name, location and operating hours. The system validates and stores the settings for use by the relevant modules. **(Requirement: FR-ADM-01) A3. Step 4 – Manage system parameters** The Administrator configures permitted prediction, inventory, simulation, leftover and notification parameters. These may include: Cold-start minimum-data threshold Low-stock thresholds Low-confidence threshold Simulation operating periods Leftover-handling rules Notification preferences or thresholds The system validates that the entered values are within their permitted ranges before storing them. **(Requirement: FR-ADM-02, NFR-MAI-02) A4. The system validates and stores the information for use in donation records. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-07)** A charity partner referenced by historical donation records shall be deactivated rather than permanently deleted. **A5. Step 4 – Configure external services** The Administrator selects **External Services**. The system displays the configuration status of the Weather Service, Calendar/Holiday Service and Push Notification Service. **(Requirement: FR-ADM-03)** The Administrator updates permitted service information, such as endpoint, location, service status or protected credential reference. The system validates the configuration and tests the service connection where supported. **(Requirement: FR-ADM-03)** The system stores the valid configuration securely. API credentials and service keys shall not be displayed unnecessarily or stored in the mobile application or source-code repository. **(Requirement: NFR-SEC-05) A6. Step 4 – Review system logs and audit trail** The Administrator selects **System Logs and Audit Trail**. The system displays permitted records containing the applicable actor, action, affected record, date, time and outcome. The Administrator may filter the records by date, category, user or status. **(Requirement: FR-ADM-04, NFR-DAT-03)** Viewing logs and audit records shall not modify their original contents. **Exception flows A7. Step 9 – Invalid or incomplete administrative information** If a required value is missing, incorrectly formatted or outside its permitted range, the system identifies the affected field and prevents the changes from being stored. **(Requirement: NFR-DAT-01) A8. Subflow A1 – Invalid or unauthorised role assignment** If the selected role is invalid or the Administrator does not have permission to assign it, the system rejects the change and retains the existing user role. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-04, FR-UAM-05) A9. Subflow A1 – Removal of the final active administrator** If an operation would deactivate or remove the final active System Administrator account, the system prevents the operation to ensure that system administration remains accessible. **A10. Subflow A4 – Duplicate or invalid charity partner** If the charity-partner information is invalid or duplicates an existing active record, the system requests corrected information before saving. **(Requirement: FR-LDW-07) A11. Subflow A5 – External-service connection test fails** If the external-service configuration cannot be validated, the system displays the failure reason and allows the Administrator to correct or retry the configuration. The existing valid configuration remains unchanged. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-03) A12. Steps 11–12 – Administrative update fails** If a processing or database error occurs, the system rolls back the incomplete operation. Existing settings remain unchanged, and no partial administrative update is stored. **(Requirement: NFR-REL-01) A13. Steps 1–13 – Access is unauthorised or the session expires** If the user is not an authorised System Administrator or the session has expired, the system denies access and returns the user to the appropriate screen or login page. **(Requirement: FR-UAM-01, FR-UAM-04)** |  |

### **3.4.4 Business Rules** {#3.4.4-business-rules}

Business rules define the operational constraints and decision logic that control how the Smart Bakery Food Waste Reduction System behaves. These rules ensure that demand prediction, production planning, inventory processing, POS simulation, leftover management and reporting are performed consistently. 

In the proposed system, demand prediction refers operationally to the forecast number of units expected to be sold on the next day because daily units sold are used as the current model’s target variable. Estimated demand is a simulation-derived analytical value calculated as units sold plus lost sales and is not used as the training target of the current model. 

Table 3.22 presents the principal business rules derived from the requirements analysis. 

*Table 3.22: Business Rules of the Proposed System*

| Rule ID | Category | Business rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-UAM-01 | User access | Only authenticated users shall be allowed to access the system functions. |
| BR-UAM-02 | Role control | Bakery managers shall access operational functions, while system-administration and model-management functions shall be restricted to system administrators. |
| BR-UAM-03  | Administrator access  | The final active System Administrator account shall not be deactivated or removed.  |
| BR-DP-01 | Prediction | The bakery manager shall manually initiate the generation of a next-day sales prediction. |
| BR-DP-02 | Prediction data | Each prediction shall use the latest available historical sales records together with weather, holiday and temporal information for the prediction date. |
| BR-DP-03 | Cold start | The active prediction model shall be used when sufficient valid historical sales data are available. Otherwise, the system shall use the configured cold-start method. |
| BR-DP-04 | Training target | The current prediction model shall use daily units sold as its target variable. Estimated demand shall be stored for analysis but shall not be used as the current model’s training target. |
| BR-DP-05 | Model retraining | Model retraining shall be manually initiated by the system administrator. A retrained candidate model shall not replace the active model until its evaluation results have been reviewed and it has been selected for activation. |
| BR-INV-01 | Recipe and inventory | A production recommendation shall only be generated when the required prediction, recipe and inventory information is available. |
| BR-INV-02 | Production feasibility | A system-generated production recommendation shall not exceed the maximum quantity that can be produced using the available valid ingredients. |
| BR-INV-03 | Production adjustment | The bakery manager may accept, reduce or override a recommendation. An adjusted quantity shall be valid and operationally feasible before it can be confirmed. |
| BR-INV-04 | Ingredient shortage | If available ingredients are insufficient, the system shall identify the shortages and recommend either producing a reduced quantity or restocking the required ingredients. |
| BR-INV-05 | FIFO processing | When an official POS simulation is initiated for a confirmed production decision, the system shall deduct the required ingredient quantities from the oldest valid inventory batches using FIFO before simulated sales processing begins. Expired batches shall not be used.  |
| BR-INV-06 | Duplicate deduction | Ingredients associated with the same confirmed production decision shall not be deducted from inventory more than once. |
| BR-POS-01 | Simulation date | The POS simulation shall use the current date by default and require a confirmed production decision for the selected date. |
| BR-POS-02 | Sales limit | The units sold during the simulation shall not exceed the confirmed production quantity. |
| BR-POS-03 | Lost sales | Lost sales shall be recorded when simulated customer demand exceeds the remaining available product quantity. |
| BR-POS-04 | Estimated demand | Estimated demand shall be calculated as the units sold plus lost sales. |
| BR-POS-05 | Leftovers | Leftover quantity shall be calculated as the confirmed production quantity minus the units sold. |
| BR-POS-06 | Simulation records | The system shall store daily units sold, lost sales, estimated demand, revenue and leftovers after the POS simulation is completed. |
| BR-POS-07 | Contextual factors  | Contextual factors already incorporated into the stored sales prediction shall not be applied again as demand multipliers during the POS simulation.  |
| BR-LDW-01 | Leftover allocation | The total quantity recorded as donated, wasted and unallocated shall not exceed the calculated leftover quantity for the corresponding bread category and date. |
| BR-LDW-02 | Donation | A donation record shall contain a valid quantity and an active charity partner. |
| BR-LDW-03 | Waste | A waste record shall contain a valid quantity and a reason for disposal. |
| BR-RPT-01 | Reporting | Reports shall be generated from stored operational and simulation records without modifying the original records. |
| BR-ALT-01 | Notifications | Background push notifications shall be delivered through the configured Push Notification Service when a relevant system event occurs and the user has enabled notifications. |

The identified business rules establish the constraints governing the main system processes. In particular, they ensure that predictions use appropriate data, production decisions remain feasible, inventory is processed consistently, simulation results are calculated correctly, and leftover allocations do not exceed the quantities available. These rules also provide a foundation for defining the detailed functional requirements and validating the system during testing.

The functional requirements define the system behaviours required to support bakery operations from next-day sales prediction and production planning to POS simulation, leftover handling and reporting. ## **3.6 Non-Functional Requirements**   {#3.6-non-functional-requirements}

Non-functional requirements define the quality attributes and operational constraints of the Smart Bakery Food Waste Reduction System. While functional requirements describe what the system shall perform, non-functional requirements specify how effectively, securely and reliably those functions shall operate. Table 3.24 presents the non-functional requirements and their proposed verification methods.

For performance and interface verification, the reference environment shall consist of an Android 10 or later device with at least 4 GB of RAM, a viewport of at least 360 × 640 density-independent pixels (dp), a stable network connection of at least 10 Mbps, and an available backend service. The reference single-bakery dataset shall contain up to 20 active bread categories, 365 historical daily records per category and 50 records per displayed list page.

| NFR-PER-02 | Performance | Under the defined reference environment, the system shall complete a next-day prediction or production recommendation within 15 seconds for up to 20 active bread categories and 365 historical daily records per category.  | System performance testing |
| NFR-PER-03 | Performance | Under the defined reference environment, the system shall complete a 12-hour POS simulation or generate a seven-day report for up to 20 bread categories within 30 seconds.  | System performance testing |
| NFR-SEC-01 | Security | The system shall require users to authenticate before accessing protected functions and information. | Authentication and access-control testing |

| NFR-SEC-03 | Security | User passwords shall not be stored or transmitted as plain text. | Security review |

| NFR-ACC-01 | Prediction quality | The prediction model shall be evaluated using a chronologically later test dataset that was not used for model training or model-parameter selection.  | Dataset-splitting procedure review  |
